[LNAM.2.6.3] **Controls in strings and comments — balance or reject.** Within a
string literal or a comment, every bidi embedding, override, or isolate the author
opens must be closed before that literal or comment ends. The compiler must reject an
unbalanced or unterminated bidi control sequence in a string literal or a comment.
The **non-scoping marks** `LRM`/`RLM` (`U+200E`/`200F`) and `ALM` (`U+061C`) open no
scope and so cannot spill; the compiler may permit them in string literals and
comments (they remain rejected in identifiers, [LNAM.2.6.2]). *(Trojan Source,
CVE-2021-42574: an unbalanced *scoping* control spills its reordering into the
surrounding source, so displayed code can differ from parsed code — pointed for a
rules engine, where a reordered `where` guard or a hidden negation passes human
review. A balanced scoping control is contained within the literal and remains the
legitimate way to embed an LTR run inside RTL string data.)*
